full_judgment:
Sharifuddin Chaklader, J: This rule by the judgment debtor directed against judgment and other dated 3-4-2006 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka dismissing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 90 of 2006 affirming the other dated 7-3-2006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka rejecting the application filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of2005. 

 4. Judgment debtors did not appear in the suit. Defendant No.3, Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation appeared and filed written statement. In the written statement this defendant took the plea that suit is no maintainable and further stated that this defendant sanctioned on 18-1-1984 and 25-4-1984, through sanction letter No. D- 16966/875 Taka 4,00,000 with 13% and Taka 2,00,000 with 6% interest, in total, Taka 6,00,000 to defendant No.1 to be repaid in 25 years with monthly installment of Taka 5,571.65 for constructing a house. Defendant No. 1 mortgaged the suit property with this defendant and handover original deed No. 5060 and 6075 dated 6-10-79 with some other papers to this defendant. Defendant No.1 on 19-7-1986 applied to this defendant for second charge with the plaintiff and this defendant by letter dated 31-8-1986 gave approval. Defendant No.1 did not repay monthly installments of this defendant. This defendent on 30-6-99 instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2000 for realizing Taka 14,30,431.41. In that case plaintiff of the instant suit appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement. This defendant prayed that if there be any decree passed in the instant case and if the schedule property be auctioned, in that case, at first, from the auctioned money all debts of this defendant as first charge would be paid. 

 6. Decree holder, Sonali Bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 497 of 2003 in Artha Rin Adalat, which was renumbered as Artha Rin Case No. 369 of 2005. The executing Court advertised on 21-3-2004 in daily news paper for auction selling of the decreed property. Auction was held and opposite party No.2 purchased the auctioned property. While auction purchaser went to take possession of the case land through police force on 5-10-2005, petitioners could know about the auction and ex-parte decree through their tenants and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 2005 under section 19(2) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2004 for setting aside the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 221 of 2001. The said case was fixed for maintainability on 7-3-2006. Learned Advocate for petitioner having been fell ill filed application for adjournment of the hearing on the maintainability of Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 2005. Learned Judge took up hearing of the Miscellaneous Case NO. 33 of 2005 on 7-3-2006 and rejected the application filed for adjournment. The learned Judge dismissed Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 2005 on 7-3-2006. Having being aggrieved by order dated 7-3-2006, judgment debtor petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 90 of 2006 before the learned District Judge. In the appeal, present petitioners filed application for not to sell the auctioned land to anybody, Learned Judge dismissed the appeal holding that since judgment debtors did not deposit 50% of the decreetal amount, the appeal is not maintainable. Against this order this rule. 

 8. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate with Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Advocate, submits that, petitioners being original owner of the disputed property who having not been informed about institution the original case for realization of money and after having got information about the ex parte decree and auction to maintain their own property rushed to the Court for setting aside the auction, not the decree as they are ready to pay the decreetal amount as such, Court should allow their prayer on taking the decreetal amount, as in that case neither the Sonali Bank nor the Bangladesh House Building Corporation nor the auction purchaser suffer any loss as Bangladesh House Building Corporation and Sonali Bank are not want to grub the property but they will be satisfied if their money be secured which the judgment debtor petitioner are ready to deposit at any moment. The learned Advocates further submits that the auction purchaser just after purchase in auction of the property entered into agreement for selling the suit property with a third party, as such, the auction purchaser purchased the suit property for not to use and live there but to make profit of the same. Learned Advocate next submits that, execution case was filed without complying with the requirement of law as no receipt of acknowledgement due accompanied with the filing of execution case to prove that judgment debtors were notified person. Learned Advocate submits that petitioners challenge the order passed by the trial Court rejecting the application filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in appeal but the appeal was dismissed on the ground for nonpayment of 50% of decreetal amount which is an order not supported by law as section 61 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain referred to two options i.e. either to set aside the decree and in that case, deposit of 50% decreetal amount is a must and next, to set aside auction sale maintaining the decree where 50% of the decreetal amount is not required to be paid, learned District Judge totally misread the provision of law in dismissing the appeal of the judgment debtor thereby refuse to place their case. Learned Advocate further submits that in putting the suit property in auction no notice was served upon the petitioners as such, auction was held after practicing fraud upon judgment debtor as well as upon the Court. Learned Advocate further submits that, in holding auction, Court is bound to act as per provisions of section 30 and 33 of Ain, 2003 which having not be complied with the entire proceeding relating to auction of the suit property is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate relying on the decision of Abdul Jalil vs Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, 41 DLR (AD) 109 submits that on the facts of the instant case this decision is applicable as in that case judgment debtor was allowed to retain the property on payment of decreetal amount giving soletium to the auction purchaser. 

 10. Mr. Jamir Uddin Sirker, learned Advocate, appearing for the auction purchaser, submits that, his client did not do any wrong as he is a bonafide purchaser of the suit property in auction pursuant to a notification published in daily newspaper pursuant to the decree obtained from a competent Court and also pursuant to the order passed in execution case, as such, auction purchase and delivery possession as made together with the judgment passed in original case and execution case should not be disturbed. 

 11. Mr. Jamir Uddin Sirker with Mr. Nowshed Jamir, Learned Advocates submits that, against the ex-parte decree obtained in original case dated 15-10-2005 judgment debtors filed Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2005, and Writ Petition No. 7705 of 2005 where the judgment debtors did not mooted the question as to service of summons in original suit as such, this question cannot be reopened as on this question Writ Petition is pending. Learned Advocate, on referring to the case of Korea Bangladesh Food Products Limited vs National Bank Limited reported in 13 MLR 253 where it has been held that:- 

 12. It appears from the record that in course of appeal the defendant was negotiating with the bank and the purchaser to sell the auction property and the defendant will pay up the entire decreetal amount at a time to the bank and he will also pay to the auction purchaser the amount together with interest. Thus, the High Court Division showed unwillingness to accept his submission to dispose of this Miscellaneous appeal as the provision for filing the appeal has not been complied with. It further appears from the record that in the absence of 50% of the decreetal amount deposit to prefer this appeal there is no existence of appeal in the eye of law", appellant must deposit 50% of the decreetal amount as such, learned District Judge committed no illegality in dismissing the appeal as it not maintainable. Learned Advocate further submits that the Appellate Division in the aforesaid 13 MLR case held that any appeal filed against any decision of Artha Rin Adalat is required to pay 50% of the decreetal amount. Learned Advocate further submits that, in the case of Sonali Bank vs Artha Rin Adalat, 15 MLR (AD) 20 = 62 DLR (AD) 231, it has been held that the execution proceeding ends with the completion of auction process in respect of mortgaged property, as such, at present when the auction process completed and delivery of auction land has already been given it cannot be re-opened. Learned Advocate further submits that although House Building Finance Corporation order and Artha Rin Adalat Ain are special law giving supremacy of the laws over all other laws prevailing but since Artha Rin Adalat Ain being later and when there is a conflict between two special laws, provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain shall prevail as such the decision reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109 has no manner of application on the facts of the instant case. 

 On the pleadings of the parties following questions calls for determination. At first, whether the ex-parte decree against the judgment debtors petitioners was passed lawfully; next, whether the execution proceeding pursuant to the ex-parte decree was legal; next, when original owner wanted to retain the case property by paying decreetal amount, whether relief can be given on setting aside the auction sale; next, whether auction sale can be set aside when the price of the property as shown in auction was shockingly too law. 

 14. It is not denied that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, Act VII of 2003 is a special law and section 3 of the Act give supremacy of the Act over other laws. Chapter 4 deals with filing of case and also procedure of the Court. Section 7 is under Chapter- 4 speaks for service of summons. Section 7 later on amended by Act 39 of 2007 stand as:- 

 15. On a reading of this section it appears that after issuing of summons from the Court if it is not served within 15 days or service return not received within 15 days, then on the matter of service of summons Court is to take recourse of procedure of Rule 20 of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure. In original case, which we have brought by special messenger as it relevant for disposal of this rule, order No. 5 dated 4-6-2002, the case was filed on 11-2-2002, runs as- 

 16. We do not understand why the learned Judge proceed so hastily as just before end of 4th month the suit was put into ex parte decree. Facts disclose that petitioner earlier took loan from defendant No. 3 for constructing residential home. The decree was passed against the petitioners ex-parte as they did not appear in the case. Laws says that when after service of summons if anyone did not appear to contest the suit then for fare and natural justice, as pet provision of rule 19 of Order V CPC the process server is required to be examined in support of his declaration and as to service of summons. His depositions stands as evidence of fact as to the service or admitted the service of the summons. On a reading of the judgment and decree passed ex-parte against this judgment debtors we find that learned Judge did not consider whether the summons were served satisfactorily or not. It is to be borne in mind that Ain, 2003 is harsh law giving no chance to a loanee to anything if it is found that he is a defaulting party. In the instant case, as we see, not only the money but also the land together with the building petitioners are loosing by stroke of pen of the learned Judge, as such, when the law is harsh then the learned Judge should be cautious before passing any judgment taking away life and property of an individual as to whether the litigant was aware of the proceeding and whether he was given proper opportunity to place his case. Whether summons were served or not it is the process server who could satisfy the Court as such, before passing an ex parte decree, since the law is harsh, the Court must examine the process server as Court witness. Law demand that before taking everything of a litigant and put him on the road, at least, from the judgment it could gather that before drawing the last blade at least Court is justify that all the required procedure of law have been satisfactorily complied with. When the law is harsh the principle of natural justice will have to follow as an abandoned caution i.e. the Court acted in equity, in honesty and rightly . 

 18. In the case of Md Nur Islam vs Agrani Bank, 1 MLR 373, it has been held that- 

 "Deposit of 50% decreetal amount in both the cases either in an application for setting aside an ex parte decree or in an appeal is necessary. 

 19. The Artha Rin Adalat Act specifically provides for only two remedies against an ex parte decree. It is either by an application or by an appeal; but in both the cases deposit of 50% decretal amount is necessary to avoid this deposit, it appears, the petitioner has sought a short-cut by invoking section 151 of the CPC which is not applicable in such a situation. 

 21. Generally it appears that if anybody challenge any decree then he will have to pay 50% of the decreetal amount as provided under section 41 of the Act of Ain, 2003 but in the instant case, it appears that, judgment debtor petitioners did not challenge the decree rather they want to maintain the decree but they have challenge the auction proceeding. The appeal is from an order passed on an application filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. When a decree has been passed, ex parte or contested, the judgment debtor can challenge the decree by filing an appeal and as per law he must deposit 50% of the decreetal amount. But, when the judgment debtor challenge the auction sale keeping the decree in tact and want to maintain the decree than he is not required to deposit 50% of the decreetal amount as the judgment debtors are not aggrieved by the decree. Since the judgment debtors did not challenge the decree rather they want to maintain the decree and prayed for setting aside the auction sale so that they can maintain their property, it is our considered view that, 50% of decreetal amount is not required to be filed as required under section 41 of the Act. 

 24. Learned Advocate next submits that, auction property was sold shockingly at a very low price at Taka 40,00,000 and referred to the schedule to the execution case. Let us quote the schedule of the property sold. 

 It appears that, 4 kathas equivalent of 10.50 decimals of land was sold at Banani Model Town at Taka 40,00,000 itself show that some mischievous hand pressurized in selling of this property as even a 'chhatak' of land at Banani Model Town could not be sold in 2005 at such low price. Learned Advocate on drawing our attention to the fact that auction notice as per provision of law was not affixed in notice board of the Court and that holding of auction was not informed in the locality by beat of drums shows that some under hand tricks have been adopted in selling the property in auction. 

 25. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that, judgment debtors being the real owners of the property and auction money being at very low they are ready to pay the entire decreetal money in order to maintain their property and relied on the decision of Abdul Jalil vs BHBFC, 41 DLR (AD) 109. In that case, House Building Finance Corporation got decree for realization of Taka 6,83,657.70 and the property was sold in auction. The original owner i.e. petitioner Abdul Jalil filed objection in holding auction upon which the learned District Judge on realising Taka 1,00,000 on the next date on 14-9-1987, by order dated 13-9-1987, postpone the sale subject to payment of balance amount by 10-11-1987. Petitioner Abdul Jalil moved vainly before the High Court in revision and thereafter, move the Appellate Division and while the matter was moved before the Appellate Division the petitioner Abdul Jalil paid the entire decreetal amount. Meanwhile property was allowed to sell in auction and auction was closed as the auction purchaser purchased the auction property at Taka 10,10,000 and odd. The Appellate Division set aside the auction sale on the observation that when the original owner is eager to maintain his property by satisfying the decree, he can do that subject to soletium paid to the auction purchaser. 

 28. There is another obstacle in executing the decree. In the decree both the loan of Sonali Bank and House Building Finance Corporation have been amalgamated in one decree but as per provision of president's Order 7 of 1973, the loan of House Building Finance Corporation cannot be realised through Artha Rin Adalat constituted under Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 or 2003 as House Building Finance Corporation order itself provides mode of realization of loan under Article 27. In the case of Jahan Ara Akhtar Begum vs BHBFC, 47 DLR 158it has been held that "We are of the view that the cases for realization of loan of the House Building Finance Corporation shall be instituted in the Court of the learned District Judge and the same would be heard and disposed of by the learned District Judge, according to the provision of Article 27 of President's Order 7 of 1978". This judgment was affirmed by the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of BHBFC vs Jahan Ara Akhtar, 49 DLR (AD) 80 where it has been held. 

 30. Provisions of section 5(1) of Artha Rin Adalat Act are very clear and, as such, the cases of the House Building Finance Corporation for realization of loan cannot be tried by the Artha Rin Adalat and if it is done, it will be wholly without jurisdiction. 

 32. As far as the present case is concerned the appellant already brought the proceedings under article 27 of President's Order No.7 of 1973. These proceedings cannot be transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat which has jurisdiction to try a suit and not proceedings under article 27. Notwithstanding the promulgation of the Act, the proceedings under article 27 can continue and we understand that this is that the High Court Division has really intended to convey although at places an impression has been given that a financial institution has to follow the special provision or procedure as provided in the relevant law for realization of loan and a suit under the Act for the said purpose will be without jurisdiction. We are, however, inclined to think that the High Court Division expressed itself keeping in view the facts of the present case only and its observations are meant to govern the case in hand and not generally. The appellant's interpretation of section 5(1) read with the proviso is found to be unacceptable." 

 35. There is another factor which, according to us, very vital i.e. whether the execution case was filed within prescribed period mentioned in the Ain, 2003. 

 37. On a reading of the law it appears that, for filing execution case, 180th day is the penultimate date and if no execution case be filed within this period then as per sub-section 2 the execution case will be dismissed as barred by limitation. Sub-section 3 provides that after dismissal of the execution case under sub-section 2, then as per provision of Sub-section 3, within 1 (one) year thereafter if execution case be not filed then the same will be dismissed. At present Sub-section 4 is not required for consideration. In the instant case in our hand the decree was passed on 29-8-2002 and as per section 28(1) execution case ought to be filed within 28-2-2003 but we find it was filed on 27-10-2003. If we give benefit of taking certified copy, then it appears that application for certified copy was filed on 27-1-2003 i.e. almost after 5 months, i.e. beyond the period for filing application for certified copy, which was obtained on 12-4-2003. Even from 12-4-2003 i.e. date of obtaining certified copy, the execution case was tiled beyond period of limitation as 180th day expired on 11-10-2003 but execution case was filed even thereafter on 21-10-2003 and legally it is more than 14 months from the date of ex-parte decree. As per provision section 28 of Ain, 2003, the Court should dismissed the execution case and as per sub-section 3, from the date of dismissal, decree holder could tile the decree for execution within 1(one) year thereafter. But nothing has so far been done lawfully and it stands the execution case as filed was filed beyond the period of limitation but the learned Judge executed the decree through execution case and the property was sold which is totally in violation of special law. We find the entire proceeding of execution case is barred by limitation and without jurisdiction as such, from the date of filing of the execution case upto selling of the property in auction, entirely was done without jurisdiction, illegally, malafide and arbitrarily with a motive. We find that execution case has filed illegally and no auction could be held on this execution proceeding. We find substance in the rule. 

 40. Before parting with the decision and lift our pen, we have considered the case of the opposite party-auction purchaser as he purchased the suit property in auction bonafide at Taka 40.00,000. Auction purchaser will get back the money from the Court with admitted Bank interest from the Bank. We are directing the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Dhaka to refund the money to the auction purchaser with interest within 30 days from the date of receipt of this order.
